analysis: Integration of five batch analyses. The PR adds a typed missingUserQuery error: Qwen35TemplateFix.validateUserQuery is called from ChatTemplateFixes.normalizeMessages, and ProviderLoop+ErrorMapping.swift maps it to a 400 client error (reason .clientError, code .invalidRequest). Qwen 3.5/3.6/3.8 and Bonsai 2 histories with no user turn beyond <tool_response> wrappers are now rejected before rendering instead of causing a template_render 500. The error message is static and content-free, and the sanitized failure path returns only closed enums, a status and bounded usage. So there is no plaintext leak on the provider-to-coordinator wire (A-001, T-008, TB-002). The change adds no crypto, attestation, authorization, key-handling or prefix-cache (T-041) surface. Docs in docs/architecture/inference.md are descriptive and make no production-qualification claims. The prefix-cache statements (sampler excluded from cache identity, SSD default for Bonsai 9B) match the T-041 posture and do not widen at-rest exposure. Non-security observations: validateUserQuery matches modelType exactly, without trim or lowercase, so a differently-cased model_type falls back to the old 500. Only String content is inspected, which fails safe. Coverage limits: the raw Qwen35TemplateFixes.swift diff was seen only through unit 3 analysis, the head text of the docs is partly truncated, and the coordinator's handling of 400 versus 500 is platform-owned and out of scope. No supported security findings, and I found no cross-batch contradictions.
